- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Le Verrier sent his predictions to German astronomer Johann Gottfried Galle, who then used them to discover the new planet, which was named Neptune.

- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] Example 1: Higgs Boson - The Higgs boson is a subatomic particle predicted by the Standard Model of particle physics, first proposed by physicist Peter Higgs in 1964, discovered in 2012 at the Large Hadron Collider.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] Example 2: General Relativity - Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity predicted the bending of light by gravity, observed during a solar eclipse in 1919.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] Example 3: Plate Tectonics - The theory of plate tectonics was first proposed in the 1960s, with evidence from seismology, paleomagnetism, and other fields confirming the theory decades later.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] Example 4: Black Holes - The idea of black holes was first proposed by physicist John Michell in the late 18th century, with their existence confirmed by observational evidence in the 1960s.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] Example 5: DNA Structure - The double helix structure of DNA was first proposed by James Watson and Francis Crick in 1953, confirmed through experimental evidence several years later, with contributions from Rosalind Franklin and others.
